metrics.label: Population
metrics.description: Total resident population at the 2022 census.

metrics.label: Under 18
metrics.description: Share of residents younger than 18.

metrics.label: Age 18-29
metrics.description: Share of residents aged 18 to 29.

metrics.label: Age 30-49
metrics.description: Share of residents aged 30 to 49.

metrics.label: Age 50-59
metrics.description: Share of residents aged 50 to 59.

metrics.label: Age 60+
metrics.description: Share of residents aged 60 and older.

metrics.label: Foreign nationals
metrics.description: Share of residents who are not German citizens.

metrics.label: Migration background
metrics.description: Share of residents with a migration background - includes naturalized citizens and their children, so it's broader than (and always ≥) foreign-national share.

metrics.label: Avg. household size
metrics.description: Average number of people living in the same household.

metrics.label: Single/two-family homes
metrics.description: Share of residential buildings that are single- or two-family houses, rather than larger apartment blocks - a rough density/urbanization proxy.

metrics.label: Total dwellings
metrics.description: Total number of housing units (not people).

metrics.label: Vacancy rate
metrics.description: Share of dwellings standing empty.

metrics.label: Owner-occupied
metrics.description: Share of dwellings lived in by their owner, as opposed to rented out.

metrics.label: Avg. rent
metrics.description: Average asking rent per square meter, cold (excluding utilities/heating).

metrics.label: Avg. gross wage
metrics.description: Average gross wage per employee, from official regional accounts (VGRdL) - before tax, and averaged across full- and part-time work.

metrics.label: Avg. household income
metrics.description: Average disposable household income (after taxes and transfers), from official regional accounts (VGRdL).

metrics.label: Median income (INKAR)
metrics.description: The middle income value (half earn more, half less) - less skewed by very high earners than an average. Exact income concept/period not confirmed against a codebook, see README.

metrics.label: GDP per capita
metrics.description: Total economic output produced in the county, divided by its population - a measure of local economic activity, not resident income (commuters can inflate it).

metrics.label: Tax capacity (Steuerkraft)
metrics.description: A municipality's own-source tax revenue capacity per resident - used in Germany's fiscal equalization system between richer and poorer areas.

metrics.label: Unemployment rate
metrics.description: Share of the civilian labor force registered as unemployed.

metrics.label: Industry employment share
metrics.description: Share of employment in manufacturing/industry, as opposed to services or agriculture - a deindustrialization proxy when tracked over time.

metrics.label: Commuter balance
metrics.description: Net commuters per 1,000 residents. Positive means more people commute IN for work than commute out (a job center); negative means the reverse (a bedroom community).

metrics.label: Foreign national share
metrics.description: Share of residents who are not German citizens (county-level, INKAR source - compare with the municipality-level Zensus figure, which may differ slightly in methodology).

metrics.label: In-migration rate
metrics.description: People moving INTO the county per 1,000 residents, per year (from elsewhere in Germany or abroad).

metrics.label: Out-migration rate
metrics.description: People moving OUT of the county per 1,000 residents, per year.

metrics.label: Asylum seekers
metrics.description: Asylum seekers registered in the county, per 1,000 residents.

metrics.label: Rent price
metrics.description: Average rent per square meter (INKAR source - compare with the municipality-level Zensus rent figure, which may differ slightly in methodology).

metrics.label: Over-indebtedness rate (Schuldnerquote)
metrics.description: Share of adults with unmanageable debt (more liabilities than they can realistically repay) - a financial-distress indicator distinct from income level.
